scenario: API Gateway auth-api-prod shows 34,000 failed authentication attempts in 30 minutes. GuardDuty flags as brute force attack against customer-facing authentication endpoint. Security team escalates for incident response.
why_misclassified: EC-06 (CIDR-gated + normal OAuth pattern): High auth failure rates are expected in multi-tenant SaaS OAuth flows. Failed attempts originate from known OAuth client IPs during token refresh storms when access tokens expire simultaneously after a deployment. Not brute force.
detection_signal: GuardDuty: UnauthorizedAccess:IAMUser/MaliciousIPCaller — 34,000 HTTP 401s in 30 min on auth-api-prod
ground_truth: Token expiry storm: deployment at 14:00 UTC caused simultaneous token expiration for 8,400 clients. Each client retries with expired token before discovering new token required. Pattern matches post-deployment spikes in past 12 deployments.
remediation_impact: Blocking authentication endpoint during OAuth token refresh storm would lock out all 8,400 customers simultaneously.

scenario: Kubernetes network policy scanner flags EKS cluster saas-prod as having insufficient namespace isolation — pods in customer-tenant-A namespace can reach customer-tenant-B namespace via service DNS. Flagged as multi-tenant lateral movement risk.
why_misclassified: EC-08 (VPC-bounded namespace isolation): Service mesh (Istio) enforces AuthorizationPolicy that restricts inter-namespace communication to only the platform's internal service bus. Despite DNS resolution capability, all actual HTTP connections require mTLS certificate from the requesting namespace's service account.
detection_signal: Network policy analysis: customer-tenant-* namespaces have no NetworkPolicy blocking inter-namespace DNS. Lateral movement path identified.
ground_truth: Istio AuthorizationPolicy deny-cross-tenant enforces source namespace restrictions. DNS resolution ≠ connectivity. mTLS required for all service-to-service calls. No cross-tenant data accessible even if DNS resolves.
remediation_impact: Adding NetworkPolicy to block inter-namespace DNS would break the platform service discovery mechanism that coordinates tenant operations.

scenario: IAM role saas-cicd-deploy-role has iam:PassRole, ec2:*, ecs:*, s3:*, and ecr:* permissions across production. Scanner flags CRITICAL for deployment role with broad permissions that could be used for privilege escalation.
why_misclassified: EC-09 (deployment automation — not overprivilege): Broad IAM role is intentional for the deployment automation pipeline. Role is assumed only by GitHub Actions OIDC federation with condition StringEquals token.actions.githubusercontent.com:aud sts.amazonaws.com AND StringLike repo:saas-org/platform:*. Not assumable by humans.
detection_signal: IAM role saas-cicd-deploy-role: iam:PassRole, ec2:*, s3:* on Resource:*. CRITICAL overpermission.
ground_truth: Role assumable only via OIDC federation from saas-org/platform GitHub repo. No human IAM users have AssumeRole permission. iam:PassRole scoped to deployment-specific role ARNs via condition. Permission boundary limits deployment scope.
remediation_impact: Restricting deployment role would break the CI/CD pipeline for 380 microservices, halting all production deployments.

scenario: CSPM flags Lambda function saas-api-gateway-v2 for having rate limiting disabled — scanner detects no throttling configuration on the API Gateway stage. Rate limiting is a SOC 2 availability control requirement.
why_misclassified: EC-03 (disabled feature actually controlled elsewhere): Rate limiting is implemented via LaunchDarkly feature flag system that applies per-tenant rate limits dynamically. The API Gateway throttle is intentionally disabled to allow the application-layer rate limiter (more granular) to control traffic.
detection_signal: API Gateway saas-api-prod stage: ThrottlingBurstLimit=0, ThrottlingRateLimit=0 (no throttling configured)
ground_truth: Application-layer rate limiter in saas-api-gateway-v2 Lambda implements per-tenant, per-endpoint rate limits via Redis token bucket algorithm. Limits configurable per customer plan. API Gateway throttle disabled to prevent double-limiting.
remediation_impact: Enabling API Gateway throttle would apply a single global limit across all tenants, breaking premium tier customers' higher rate limits.

scenario: CSPM flags developer sandbox account 987654321012 for multiple HIGH misconfigurations: public S3 buckets, open security groups, no MFA for IAM users. Finding aggregated as HIGH risk environment.
why_misclassified: EC-21 (intentionally permissive sandbox): Sandbox account is for developer experimentation per documented policy. No customer data, no production access, isolated VPC with no peering to production. Permissive configurations are intentional to enable rapid prototyping without security overhead.
detection_signal: Sandbox account: 12 HIGH findings including public S3, open SGs, no MFA. Account 987654321012.
ground_truth: Account tagged Purpose=developer-sandbox, DataClassification=none. SCPs block production account access. No real data. AWS Control Tower guardrail prevents any IAM trust relationships to production accounts.
remediation_impact: Hardening sandbox accounts to production standards defeats the purpose of developer sandboxes, slowing feature development velocity.

scenario: API Gateway endpoint /webhooks/receive allows POST from 0.0.0.0/0. Scanner flags HIGH for unauthenticated open ingress endpoint that could receive arbitrary payloads.
why_misclassified: EC-16 (edge-shielded with HMAC): Webhook endpoint is intentionally public to receive third-party platform webhooks (GitHub, Slack, Stripe). All payloads verified via HMAC-SHA256 signature validation before processing. Invalid signatures rejected with 401.
detection_signal: API Gateway: POST /webhooks/receive — no API key, no IAM auth, public endpoint from 0.0.0.0/0
ground_truth: Webhook receiver validates X-Signature-256 HMAC header against registered webhook secrets. Payload processing only occurs after signature verification. Unsigned requests rejected before any business logic executed.
remediation_impact: Adding authentication to webhook endpoint would break all third-party webhook integrations for 14,000 SaaS customers.

scenario: CSPM flags Cloud Run service saas-graphql-api for having GraphQL introspection enabled in production. Security guidance recommends disabling introspection in production to prevent schema enumeration.
why_misclassified: EC-03 (intentionally enabled feature for developer experience): This is a developer platform SaaS product where GraphQL introspection is a documented feature for customers building integrations. Disabling introspection would break the GraphQL playground used by 8,200 developer customers.
detection_signal: GraphQL endpoint: __schema introspection query returns full schema. Cloud Run service saas-graphql-api.
ground_truth: Introspection intentionally enabled per product design — developer experience feature. All GraphQL queries still require authentication. Introspection only reveals schema, not data. Schema is already documented in public API docs.
remediation_impact: Disabling introspection breaks the API explorer tool used by 8,200 developer customers, a core product feature.

scenario: Vulnerability scanner reports 2x findings for CVE-2024-45338 in service saas-auth-service — one for the stable deployment and one for the canary deployment receiving 5% traffic. Security team opens 2 priority tickets.
why_misclassified: EC-12 (canary/shadow duplicate): Stable and canary deployments run side-by-side as different Kubernetes deployments but represent the same service version in this case (canary is testing config change only, same container image). One CVE finding should generate one remediation ticket.
detection_signal: CVE-2024-45338 HIGH in saas-auth-service-stable:v4.2.1 AND saas-auth-service-canary:v4.2.1 (same image tag)
ground_truth: Both deployments use identical container image saas-auth-service:v4.2.1. Single image build, dual deployment. Patching one image version fixes both deployments simultaneously. Deduplication by image digest would collapse to 1 finding.
remediation_impact: Duplicate tickets consume 2x engineer time for a single-image remediation. Canary deployment label should not generate independent CVE findings.

scenario: Service mesh TLS scanner flags GKE cluster saas-gke-prod for 15-minute windows with certificate validation failures during certificate rotation. Finding reports HIGH for intermittent mTLS enforcement gaps.
why_misclassified: EC-32 (mTLS with cert rotation gaps): Certificate rotation uses a rolling update that creates a brief overlap window where both old and new certificates are valid. During rotation, services temporarily accept connections with either cert. This is the intentional graceful rotation design, not a gap.
detection_signal: Istio cert rotation: 15-minute windows where both old and new certificates accepted. mTLS validation: PERMISSIVE during rotation.
ground_truth: Cert rotation uses PERMISSIVE mode for 15 minutes to allow gradual rollover without service disruption. After rotation completes, mode returns to STRICT. Zero connection drops during rotation. Window documented in cert-rotation-runbook.md.
remediation_impact: Eliminating rotation grace period would cause cascading connection failures across all 380 microservices during cert rotation.

scenario: Kubernetes RBAC scanner finds ClusterRole saas-platform-operator with get/list/watch/patch on all resource types in all namespaces. Assigned to the platform SRE team. Flagged CRITICAL for overpermissive RBAC.
why_misclassified: EC-09 (deployment automation role): Platform operator role is intentional for SRE automation scripts that manage cross-tenant operations (node draining, cluster upgrades, monitoring). All API calls logged to audit trail. Role bound to named service accounts used by specific automation tooling only.
detection_signal: ClusterRole saas-platform-operator: verbs=[get,list,watch,patch,delete] resources=[*] apiGroups=[*]. CRITICAL.
ground_truth: ClusterRoleBinding restricts to 2 service accounts: saas-sre-automation and saas-upgrade-controller. Both have CloudTrail-equivalent API audit logging. Human SREs have more restrictive roles — this broad role is automation-only.
remediation_impact: Restricting automation role would break cluster upgrade automation and monitoring tooling used by SRE for 24/7 platform operations.

scenario: ECR scan flags production container image saas-api:v8.4.2 for CVE-2024-21538 (ReDoS in jest) as HIGH. Container is the production API service.
why_misclassified: EC-43 (build-time dep): jest is in devDependencies used only for unit testing. The Docker build uses multi-stage build with --production flag for the final stage, excluding all devDependencies from the runtime image. jest is not present in the production container layer.
detection_signal: ECR image scan: jest@29.7.0 with CVE-2024-21538 in saas-api:v8.4.2 image
ground_truth: Multi-stage Dockerfile: Stage 1 (builder) includes devDeps for testing. Stage 2 (production) copies only src/ and runs npm ci --production. jest not present in final image. Scanner scanning the build cache layer, not the production layer.
remediation_impact: Patching jest in production image has no effect — it's not in the image. Upgrade in devDependencies sufficient and unurgent.

scenario: CSPM flags RDS instance saas-customer-db-prod as CRITICAL for publicly_accessible=true. Database contains multi-tenant SaaS customer data with PII and business records.
why_misclassified: EC-37 (publicly_accessible in private subnet): Flag set to true to enable DNS hostname resolution from peered VPCs (cross-region replication setup). Instance is in a private subnet with no IGW route. Security group allows only port 5432 from application tier security group.
detection_signal: RDS saas-customer-db-prod: publicly_accessible=true in subnet subnet-private-saas-1a
ground_truth: Private subnet subnet-private-saas-1a routes only to VPC peering connection. No NAT gateway or IGW in route table. publicly_accessible=true enables cross-region read replica DNS resolution per AWS documentation for multi-region RDS.
remediation_impact: Setting publicly_accessible=false breaks cross-region read replica DNS resolution, disabling disaster recovery read replica in us-west-2.

scenario: IAM role saas-marketplace-metering-role allows cross-account access from AWS account 287250355862 (AWS Marketplace). Scanner flags HIGH for external account access.
why_misclassified: EC-27 (intra-org trust — AWS service integration): Account 287250355862 is AWS's own Marketplace Metering Service account. This trust relationship is required for AWS Marketplace billing integration and is documented in AWS's own integration guide.
detection_signal: IAM role trust policy: aws:PrincipalAccount=287250355862 on saas-marketplace-metering-role
ground_truth: 287250355862 is AWS Marketplace Metering Service. Trust required for usage metering API calls from AWS Marketplace to SaaS account. Role allows only aws-marketplace:MeterUsage on specific resource. Documented AWS Marketplace integration requirement.
remediation_impact: Removing trust relationship disables AWS Marketplace billing, cutting off revenue from 340 enterprise customers purchasing via AWS Marketplace.

scenario: CSPM flags 120 EC2 instances in staging account as unauthorized compute — identical launch pattern suggests potential cryptomining. All instances launched by same IAM role in 5 minutes.
why_misclassified: EC-10 (ephemeral load test): Instances are Locust worker nodes for a pre-launch load test. All tagged LoadTestId=pre-launch-2026-01-28, TTL=3h. SRE team's scheduled load test to validate capacity before public launch.
detection_signal: 120 c5.xlarge instances launched from single IAM role saas-load-test-role in staging account in 5 minutes
ground_truth: Locust distributed load test for pre-launch validation. All instances auto-terminate after test completion. No internet-facing exposure from staging. IAM role restricted to staging account via SCP.
remediation_impact: Terminating load test would invalidate capacity planning data needed for launch readiness sign-off.

scenario: DLP scan flags BigQuery table saas-analytics-dev.user_events as containing PII — 5M event records with email, user_id, and session data. GDPR finding generated for dev environment.
why_misclassified: EC-20 (synthetic data): Dev environment populated with Mimesis-generated synthetic user profiles. Email field contains synthetic addresses @users.saas-test.invalid, user_ids are sequential integers starting at 1B (real prod IDs are UUID4), session data has realistic but randomized patterns.
detection_signal: DLP: email pattern in saas-analytics-dev.user_events.email_address (5M rows)
ground_truth: Synthetic data pipeline (saas-data-generator) populates dev from Mimesis library. .saas-test.invalid domain is organization-owned and non-deliverable. No real user emails. user_id range 1000000000+ reserved for synthetic data.
remediation_impact: Restricting synthetic dev data access blocks analytics engineering from developing and testing new event processing features.

scenario: Artifact Registry scan reports CVE-2023-4863 (libwebp heap overflow, AV:N/AC:L) in distroless Python image used by saas-ml-inference service. Scanner reports HIGH requiring patch.
why_misclassified: EC-29 (distroless — AV:N but no attack surface): While AV:N, the libwebp library is not reachable from the ML inference API. The service accepts JSON requests only. libwebp in the base image is never imported or called by any Python code in the application.
detection_signal: Distroless Python image: libwebp 1.2.4 with CVE-2023-4863 CVSS 8.8 HIGH (AV:N)
ground_truth: ML inference service accepts only JSON requests via HTTP. No image processing code paths. libwebp present as OS library in distroless base but no Python import references it. Package reachability: 0%.
remediation_impact: Rebuilding distroless image to upgrade unreachable libwebp adds CI/CD overhead with no security benefit.

scenario: IAM role saas-emergency-access with AdministratorAccess has a trust policy allowing specific IAM users to assume it with MFA condition. CSPM generates no finding due to break-glass exemption. Assessment: correctly classified.
why_misclassified: This is a correctly classified break-glass role. AdministratorAccess is appropriate for emergency access with MFA condition, documented procedures, and CloudTrail monitoring. Break-glass exemption correctly applied.
detection_signal: Role saas-emergency-access: AdministratorAccess. Trust: MFA required, specific IAM users only. Break-glass exemption tag applied.
ground_truth: Legitimate break-glass role per SOC 2 CC6.3 requirement. MFA condition enforced. All assumptions logged to CloudTrail and reviewed weekly. Usage rate: 0.3/month average. Properly exempted.
remediation_impact: No remediation needed — this is a correctly functioning break-glass role.

scenario: CSPM reports 4 HIGH findings for CloudWatch Log Group encryption not enabled — one each in us-east-1, us-west-2, eu-west-1, ap-northeast-1. Security team opens 4 tickets.
why_misclassified: EC-38 (cross-region duplicate): Each region's finding represents the same underlying policy gap (no CMK for log group encryption). A single policy fix (apply CMK to log groups via CloudFormation StackSet) resolves all 4 regions. 4 tickets for 1 remediation action.
detection_signal: 4 regional findings: /aws/lambda/saas-api log group missing KMS encryption in 4 regions
ground_truth: Same Lambda function deployed across 4 regions via StackSet. Log group CMK configuration gap affects all regions equally. StackSet update fixes all simultaneously. Deduplication by resource type + finding type + account would collapse to 1 ticket.
remediation_impact: 4x engineer time for 1 StackSet update, consuming analyst capacity that could address other findings.

scenario: Security group saas-internal-api-sg allows inbound port 443 from 0.0.0.0/0. No finding because group is tagged team=platform and platform team findings are suppressed during a feature freeze (automated suppression to reduce noise).
why_misclassified: EC-49 (tag suppression masking real issue): Feature freeze suppression was intended for low-severity config drift. The security group was modified by IaC accident during the freeze to expose an internal API endpoint to the internet. Suppression hides a real CRITICAL exposure.
detection_signal: Security group saas-internal-api-sg in suppressed state (tag team=platform, freeze_mode=true)
ground_truth: SG modified 3 days ago via Terraform apply error. Internal API (saas-internal-control-plane) now reachable from internet on port 443. Control plane has no external authentication — relies on VPC network isolation. Feature freeze suppression applied at wrong granularity.
remediation_impact: Internal control plane API exposed to internet without authentication. Real CRITICAL with potential for full tenant data access.

scenario: EKS cluster saas-prod RBAC configuration shows compliant per CSPM (last scan 12 days ago). Engineer manually added a ClusterRoleBinding for debugging 8 days ago giving their personal service account cluster-admin.
why_misclassified: EC-24 (stale scan drift): Manual RBAC change occurred between 14-day scan cycles. Real-time change detection for EKS RBAC not configured. cluster-admin binding persists unreported.
detection_signal: Last CSPM RBAC scan: 12 days ago (clean). Manual ClusterRoleBinding created 8 days ago not reflected.
ground_truth: ClusterRoleBinding debug-sa-admin grants cluster-admin to engineer service account. Created for incident debugging. Never removed post-incident. Full cluster access persists for non-operator service account.
remediation_impact: Engineer service account with cluster-admin on production cluster. Multi-tenant data accessible via kubectl exec or API server.

scenario: Lambda function saas-billing-engine uses vendored Stripe SDK fork. SBOM marks as vendor-managed, skipping CVE analysis. Vendored copy is 11 months old.
why_misclassified: EC-42 (vendored fork not patched): CVE-2024-32002 disclosed 4 months ago in stripe-node upstream. The internal fork was taken before the CVE and was never updated. Scanner assumes vendored = patched without verification.
detection_signal: vendor/stripe-node/ in saas-billing-engine Lambda. SBOM: vendor-managed, CVE scan skipped.
ground_truth: vendor/stripe-node/lib/http-client.js uses node-fetch 2.6.7 with CVE-2024-28849 (SSRF, HIGH). Vendored copy predates the CVE. Billing engine makes HTTP calls to Stripe API — SSRF exploitable to redirect payment API calls.
remediation_impact: SSRF in billing HTTP client potentially exploitable to redirect Stripe API calls during payment processing.

scenario: GCP emergency SA saas-emergency@saas-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com created a user-managed key via the GCP Console. CSPM does not flag because SA is in break-glass exemption. Key has Owner role.
why_misclassified: EC-28 (break-glass abuse): Break-glass exemption covers IAM role findings but accidentally also suppresses SA key creation alerts. Emergency procedure requires Workload Identity Federation, not key files. Key creation is out-of-policy.
detection_signal: Break-glass SA in exemption list. Key creation event logged to Cloud Audit Logs but not surfaced as CSPM finding.
ground_truth: SA key created outside documented break-glass procedure. Key persists after incident window. Owner-level SA key could be exfiltrated or misused. No expiration set.
remediation_impact: Persistent Owner SA key with no expiry. If exfiltrated, grants full project control including all customer data in GCP project.

scenario: ECR image saas-integrations:v3.5.0 passes all CVE checks. However, the SBOM was generated from the source package.json not the actual installed node_modules tree, missing a npm hoisting resolution difference.
why_misclassified: EC-44 (SBOM manifest vs installed tree mismatch): package.json declares axios@1.6.0 (no known CVEs at scan time). npm install resolves axios@0.27.2 for a nested dependency due to peer dependency conflict. axios@0.27.2 has CVE-2023-45857 (CSRF, HIGH). Scanner reads manifest, not resolved lockfile.
detection_signal: SBOM from package.json: axios@1.6.0 — no CVEs. ECR scan: passed.
ground_truth: package-lock.json shows axios@0.27.2 in nested node_modules/sdk-lib/node_modules/axios. This version has CVE-2023-45857. SBOM generated from top-level package.json misses nested resolution.
remediation_impact: CSRF vulnerability in HTTP client used by integration webhooks allows request forgery attacks against integrated SaaS APIs.

scenario: Cloud Run service saas-data-pipeline has CVE-2024-41110 in Docker engine used for build-time containers. Feature flag 'new-pipeline-engine=true' shows 15% rollout in LaunchDarkly. CSPM suppresses finding as flag below 20% threshold.
why_misclassified: EC-45 (partial rollout active in prod): 15% of the production data pipeline uses the vulnerable engine. 15% of customer data processing workflows touch the CVE. Threshold-based suppression is appropriate for unreleased features but not production traffic segments.
detection_signal: Feature flag new-pipeline-engine: 15% rollout. CSPM threshold: suppress below 20%. No finding.
ground_truth: 15% production rollout = ~4,500 customer pipeline runs/day on vulnerable Docker engine version. CVE-2024-41110 (container escape, CVSS 9.9) actively exploitable in the deployed configuration.
remediation_impact: Container escape vulnerability in production pipeline for 15% of customers goes undetected due to percentage threshold suppression.

scenario: Azure AD service principal saas-reporting-sp shows last sign-in 88 days ago per CSPM (PST timezone). Policy: revoke after 90 days. CSPM marks as active. SP has Contributor role on 8 Azure subscriptions.
why_misclassified: EC-48 (timezone mismatch): Azure sign-in logs are in UTC. CSPM converts to PST without DST correction. Actual UTC age: 91 days — past 90-day threshold. DST conversion error prevents flag from triggering.
detection_signal: SP last_sign_in: 2025-11-02T08:00:00Z UTC. CSPM evaluation: 88 days ago (PST calculation). Policy: 90 days. Result: active.
ground_truth: UTC calculation: 91 days since last sign-in. SP has Contributor on 8 Azure subscriptions with SaaS infrastructure. Genuinely stale but DST math keeps it 2 days under threshold.
remediation_impact: Stale Contributor SP on 8 Azure subscriptions. If credentials leaked, full infrastructure modification access.

scenario: AWS Security Hub reports LOW for 'EC2 security group allows ingress from 0.0.0.0/0 on port 22' on saas-admin-bastion. Analyst deprioritizes as LOW.
why_misclassified: EC-47 (CSP severity non-equivalence): AWS Security Hub rates SSH exposure as LOW assuming key-based auth. The SaaS admin bastion uses password authentication (keys were reset during an access issue). The actual risk is HIGH for an exposed bastion with password auth.
detection_signal: Security Hub: SSH-open-0.0.0.0/0 LOW on sg-0saas-bastion. Default severity applied.
ground_truth: Bastion sshd_config: PasswordAuthentication yes. Exposed to 0.0.0.0/0. Password auth allows brute force. Security Hub LOW assumes key-only auth which is the default assumption but not this configuration.
remediation_impact: Brute-forceable bastion with admin access to all SaaS production infrastructure. LOW SLA (90 days) allows prolonged exposure.

scenario: IAM role saas-tenant-provisioning with iam:CreateRole, iam:AttachRolePolicy, ec2:*, rds:* flagged as CRITICAL for privilege escalation risk through IAM role creation.
why_misclassified: EC-15 (permission boundary): Role has a permission boundary restricting iam:CreateRole to only roles with the saas-tenant-boundary permission boundary attached. Roles created by this role can never exceed the boundary permissions. iam:CreateRole with boundary condition prevents privilege escalation.
detection_signal: IAM role saas-tenant-provisioning: iam:CreateRole, iam:AttachRolePolicy on Resource: arn:aws:iam::*:role/tenant-*
ground_truth: iam:CreateRole has condition iam:PermissionsBoundary=arn:aws:iam::*:policy/saas-tenant-boundary required. Any created role is bounded. Privilege escalation path blocked. Tenant isolation maintained via permission boundary enforcement.
remediation_impact: Restricting tenant provisioning role would prevent automated customer onboarding, breaking the self-service tenant setup that handles 80 new customers/day.

scenario: Macie scans RDS instance saas-demo-tenant-db and finds PII in all tables — names, emails, addresses, credit card numbers in the demo_customers schema. 500K records flagged.
why_misclassified: EC-21 (synthetic demo data): Demo tenant database is populated with synthetic data for sales demos and proof-of-concept trials. All data is Faker-generated. Credit card numbers are test Stripe card numbers (4242 4242 4242 4242 pattern) — not real PANs.
detection_signal: Macie: PII detected in saas-demo-tenant-db — email, name, address, credit card number patterns (500K rows)
ground_truth: Database populated by saas-demo-seeder service using Faker and Stripe test card numbers. Email domain: @demo.saas-test.invalid. Stripe test cards are publicly documented test numbers, not real card data.
remediation_impact: Restricting demo database access would prevent sales team from demonstrating the product to prospective enterprise customers.

scenario: DLP scanner flags DynamoDB table saas-audit-logs as containing user identifiers across 280M audit records. GDPR breach potential reported.
why_misclassified: EC-22 (tokenization): DynamoDB stores user_token — a HMAC-SHA256 token derived from user_id using a platform secret. The mapping table is in a separate, more restricted service. Audit logs contain only tokens — the actual user identity cannot be derived from audit log records alone.
detection_signal: DLP: 280M DynamoDB items with field 'user_token' (32-char hex string matching identifier pattern)
ground_truth: user_token is HMAC-SHA256(user_id, platform_secret). No reverse mapping stored in DynamoDB. Deriving user identity requires the platform_secret stored separately in AWS Secrets Manager. Pseudonymization standard met.
remediation_impact: Treating HMAC tokens as PII would require rearchitecting the audit log system, breaking compliance reporting for all customers.

scenario: CSPM reports HIGH for 'CloudTrail not enabled in ap-south-1' for SaaS tenant AWS account 444555666777. SOC 2 CC7.2 audit logging requirement appears unmet.
why_misclassified: EC-19 (org-level trail): AWS Organizations trail saas-org-audit covers all regions in all member accounts. Scanner checks per-account trails only. CC7.2 satisfied by org-level trail.
detection_signal: No CloudTrail in ap-south-1 for account 444555666777
ground_truth: Org trail covers all regions. Logs stored in s3://saas-centralized-audit-logs with 7-year retention. Account is a member of the SaaS AWS organization. Org trail logs all API activity including the missing region.
remediation_impact: Duplicate per-account trails would double CloudTrail costs across 340 tenant accounts ($28K/month savings maintained).

scenario: Lambda function saas-webhook-processor flagged for CVE-2024-24783 (Go TLS) in the go1.21 Lambda managed runtime. Finding requests immediate runtime migration to go1.22.
why_misclassified: EC-36 (managed runtime shared responsibility): Go1.21 Lambda runtime is managed by AWS. TLS library vulnerabilities in the managed runtime layer are patched by AWS transparently. Customer code runs above the managed runtime.
detection_signal: Lambda saas-webhook-processor: runtime go1.21 — CVE-2024-24783 in go TLS standard library
ground_truth: AWS patches managed Lambda runtimes. CVE in standard library of managed runtime is AWS responsibility. Customer cannot patch standard library — only AWS can. AWS issued security bulletin confirming patch applied to go1.21.x runtime.
remediation_impact: Migration to go1.22 has legitimate benefits but CRITICAL urgency is misplaced — AWS already patched the managed runtime.

scenario: Azure AD scanner flags SaaS CI/CD service principal saas-pipeline-sp for not having MFA enabled. Principal has Contributor role on 4 Azure subscriptions.
why_misclassified: EC-14 (service principal programmatic auth): Service principals use certificate-based authentication (X.509 certificate stored in Azure Key Vault). MFA is a human authentication factor — not applicable to service principals using certificate auth. The certificate is the authentication equivalent of MFA for non-interactive auth.
detection_signal: Azure AD SP saas-pipeline-sp: mfa_enforced=false, azure_role=Contributor on 4 subscriptions
ground_truth: SP authenticates via X.509 certificate in Azure Key Vault with certificate rotation every 90 days. No interactive login possible. MFA requirement in Conditional Access policy explicitly excludes service principals (by design in Azure AD).
remediation_impact: MFA for service principals is technically non-functional in Azure AD. Finding generates false compliance concern.

scenario: GCP Load Balancer backend service saas-api-backend allows all source IPs. Scanner flags HIGH for open customer-facing API backend without IP restriction.
why_misclassified: EC-05 (Cloud Armor WAF-shielded): Backend service protected by Cloud Armor security policy with OWASP Top 10 rules, adaptive protection, and rate limiting per IP. Direct backend access not possible — all traffic flows through LB + Cloud Armor.
detection_signal: Backend service saas-api-backend: no IP restriction configured
ground_truth: Cloud Armor security policy saas-api-armor enforces: OWASP rules, rate limit 1000 req/IP/min, geo-block high-risk regions. Backend not directly accessible. All public traffic must traverse Cloud Armor.
remediation_impact: IP restriction on backend service is not a GCP-supported configuration for external HTTPS LB. Cloud Armor is the correct security control.

scenario: CSPM flags 6 Elastic IPs as unattached and wasteful, recommending deletion. EIPs sit idle in us-west-2 DR region.
why_misclassified: EC-07 (intentionally reserved DR IPs): EIPs are pre-configured in Route53 failover records and customer firewall allowlists. Releasing them would require customer-by-customer allowlist updates during a DR event — impractical under RTO constraints.
detection_signal: 6 EIPs unattached for 180-365 days in us-west-2. AWS Cost: $43.80/month.
ground_truth: EIPs registered in Route53 failover records. 340 enterprise customers have these IPs in their outbound firewall allowlists for saas-api connectivity. DR runbook: attach to failover load balancer within 5 minutes of failover event.
remediation_impact: Releasing DR EIPs would break disaster recovery capability and require notifying 340 enterprise customers to update firewall rules during a crisis.

scenario: Cloud Run Job saas-billing-reconciliation has CVE-2024-45491 (libexpat RCE, CVSS 9.8) flagged as HIGH. Job runs daily for 8 minutes to reconcile subscription billing.
why_misclassified: EC-33 (ephemeral batch job): Job runs 8 minutes/day in isolated VPC. libexpat used for parsing Stripe webhook XML. No external network access during execution (VPC egress restricted to Stripe API endpoint only). 8-minute daily execution window drastically limits exploitability.
detection_signal: Cloud Run Job saas-billing-reconciliation: libexpat 2.5.0 with CVE-2024-45491 CVSS 9.8
ground_truth: Job runs 8 min/day with no inbound network access. libexpat processes Stripe XML from a trusted source (HTTPS + Stripe signature verification). External attacker would need to compromise Stripe's API or conduct a MITM during the 8-minute window.
remediation_impact: Finding warrants patching but HIGH urgency overstates exploitability for an ephemeral job with no public input path.

scenario: ECS task saas-legacy-oauth-service has 12 HIGH CVEs. Service is flagged for immediate remediation. Task definition last deployed 8 months ago.
why_misclassified: EC-11 (sunset service): Service fully replaced by saas-oauth-v2 18 months ago. ECS service has desired_count=0 (no running tasks). Task definition exists as config artifact. Zero tasks means zero exposure.
detection_signal: ECS task definition saas-legacy-oauth-service:v3 has 12 HIGH CVEs in nodejs14 base image
ground_truth: ECS service desired_count=0 since 2024-07-01. No running tasks. ALB target group has 0 healthy targets. Task definition retained for rollback documentation only. Decommission ticket JIRA-SAAS-2891 pending.
remediation_impact: Emergency image patching for a service with 0 running tasks has no security impact. Decommission is the correct action.

scenario: EC2 instance saas-windows-rdgateway (Windows Server 2022) has no CVE findings. Scanner applied Linux CVE feed during a feed migration that incorrectly profiled the instance OS.
why_misclassified: EC-34 inverse (Windows CVEs missed on Windows instance): Feed migration tagged the instance as linux/x86_64 based on an AWS API response parsing error. Windows-specific CVEs including CVE-2024-38063 (TCP/IP RCE, CVSS 9.8) not applied.
detection_signal: Scanner: instance i-0saas-rdgateway OS detected as linux/x86_64. No Windows CVE feed applied.
ground_truth: Instance runs Windows Server 2022. GetConsoleOutput shows Windows boot sequence. CVE-2024-38063 (IPv6 TCP/IP stack RCE) applies to Windows Server 2022. Feed OS detection error caused miss.
remediation_impact: Critical RCE on Remote Desktop Gateway — internet-facing service — goes unpatched due to OS detection error in CVE feed.

scenario: EKS cluster saas-prod has Kyverno image signing policy. CSPM shows policy enabled. However, an engineer deployed a hotfix directly via kubectl bypassing the CI/CD pipeline and Kyverno was not enforcing during a node restart.
why_misclassified: EC-35 (admission enforcement gap): Kyverno webhook had a 4-minute unavailability window during node restart. During this window, Kyverno failurePolicy was set to Ignore (not Fail) meaning requests proceed without admission check if webhook unavailable. Unsigned image deployed.
detection_signal: Kyverno policy: enabled. CSPM: compliant. Webhook unavailability and failurePolicy not monitored.
ground_truth: Webhook failurePolicy=Ignore allowed deployment during 4-minute window. Unsigned image saas-api-hotfix:untagged-abc123 deployed. Image provenance unverifiable. FailurePolicy should be Fail for production image signing enforcement.
remediation_impact: Unsigned hotfix image in production. Supply chain integrity cannot be verified. Could be tampered or from unofficial build.

scenario: OpenSearch domain saas-search-prod has HTTP access enabled on port 9200 within VPC. Scanner flags HIGH for unencrypted HTTP access to search index containing customer data.
why_misclassified: EC-13 (app-layer encryption): All customer data is encrypted before indexing using AES-256 field-level encryption. HTTP transport exposes only ciphertext. Additionally, port 9200 is not accessible from outside the VPC — only from application tier security group.
detection_signal: OpenSearch saas-search-prod: NodeToNodeEncryption=false, HTTP port 9200 accessible within VPC
ground_truth: Field-level encryption applied before indexing. HTTP within VPC exposes only ciphertext. Security group allows 9200 only from app-tier SG. Node-to-node encryption at AWS layer is additional but not critical given application encryption.
remediation_impact: Enabling node-to-node encryption is good practice but HIGH severity overstates risk when data is already application-level encrypted.

scenario: Lambda function saas-notifications has CVE-2023-32731 (grpc RCE, CVSS 7.5) flagged via SBOM. Engineering cannot find gRPC usage in the codebase.
why_misclassified: EC-01 (ghost package): @google-cloud/pubsub SDK has grpc as transitive dependency. This Lambda uses pubsub for event streaming but via the REST transport (useGrpc: false config). gRPC code is in the dependency tree but the REST transport path is used exclusively.
detection_signal: SBOM: grpc@1.24.11 present in saas-notifications Lambda. CVE-2023-32731 HIGH.
ground_truth: pubsub client configured with clientConfig: {useGrpc: false}. REST transport used. grpc module present in node_modules but never initialized or executed. Bundle analysis: grpc code not in webpack output for REST transport path.
remediation_impact: Patching a transitive library that is never loaded has no security benefit.

scenario: ClusterRole saas-tenant-manager has create/get/list/watch/delete on all resource types in all namespaces. Assigned to the tenant management operator. Flagged HIGH for over-permissive RBAC.
why_misclassified: EC-31 (OPA/Gatekeeper compensating): Gatekeeper policy TenantResourceOwnership enforces that all resources created or modified must have the tenant-id label matching the operator's ServiceAccount annotation. Even with broad RBAC, cross-tenant operations are blocked at admission.
detection_signal: ClusterRole saas-tenant-manager: all verbs, all resources. 1 ClusterRoleBinding to saas-tenant-operator SA.
ground_truth: Gatekeeper constraint saas-tenant-isolation requires resources to match requesting SA tenant label. Cross-tenant resource creation denied at admission webhook. OPA policy reviewed by security team.
remediation_impact: Restricting RBAC to per-tenant roles would require 340 ClusterRoles and 340 ClusterRoleBindings — infeasible multi-tenant operator pattern.

scenario: GuardDuty reports LOW for EC2 instance saas-api-worker-03 communicating with a known threat actor IP. GuardDuty Malware Protection tier active — malware scan clean. Severity auto-downgraded to LOW.
why_misclassified: EC-50 (enhanced tier severity discount): GuardDuty Malware Protection tier downgrades threat findings when malware scan is clean, assuming threat intelligence is a false positive. However, the instance is communicating with a C2 IP using HTTP over port 443 — C2 beacon patterns visible in CloudWatch traffic logs.
detection_signal: GuardDuty: Recon:EC2/PortProbeUnprotectedPort LOW — malware scan clean. Severity auto-reduced.
ground_truth: Traffic analysis shows 30-second interval HTTP beacons to known C2 infrastructure 185.220.101.x. Malware scan missed the beacon implant (fileless execution). GuardDuty Malware Protection's clean scan incorrectly absolves the finding.
remediation_impact: Potential C2 beacon from production API worker goes uninvestigated at LOW priority. Real threat actor potentially present in SaaS infrastructure.

scenario: CSPM flags 22 SQS queues for not using customer-managed KMS keys. Queues are part of the event streaming backbone for the SaaS platform.
why_misclassified: EC-39 (serverless encryption nuance): SQS queues are encrypted with AWS-managed SSE-SQS keys by default. Finding is CMK absence, not encryption absence. AWS-managed encryption satisfies SOC 2 CC6.1 encryption at rest. CMK required only for queues containing CDE or PII content.
detection_signal: 22 SQS queues: KmsMasterKeyId=null (no CMK). SOC 2 encryption gap flagged.
ground_truth: AWS SSE-SQS (AES-256, AWS-managed) applied to all queues. SOC 2 encryption at rest: satisfied. 22 queues handle internal platform events (metrics, logs, notifications) — no PII or CDE content requiring CMK.
remediation_impact: Adding CMK to 22 internal event queues adds $4.4K/month KMS costs and KMS-induced latency to event processing.

scenario: IAM user saas-legacy-integration-user has access key AKIASAAS0000000001 with last_used=null. CSPM classifies as inactive/headless SA — low risk exemption applied.
why_misclassified: EC-26 (never-used key not inactive): Key created 14 months ago during vendor integration setup. Integration was abandoned but key never revoked. Key has s3:PutObject on saas-customer-data-exports bucket — never used but valid credential.
detection_signal: IAM user saas-legacy-integration-user: access key last_used=null (14 months old). CSPM: inactive, low risk.
ground_truth: Valid, never-rotated key exists with write access to customer data export bucket. Vendor integration abandoned. Key represents orphaned credential with data write access.
remediation_impact: Orphaned key with customer data write access. Credential theft or abuse could allow unauthorized data manipulation in customer export pipeline.

scenario: Azure Policy reports 4 secrets in saas-keyvault-prod with expiry dates 7-14 days past. Compliance dashboard shows non-compliant. Requires immediate rotation.
why_misclassified: EC-25 (rotation lag with grace period): All 4 secrets rotated 2 days ago. New versions are active. Old versions were disabled but retained for 14-day rollback window per rotation SOP. Scanner evaluates expiry dates including disabled versions.
detection_signal: Azure Key Vault: 4 secrets with ExpiryTime in past (7-14 days ago). Active status: Disabled.
ground_truth: New secret versions created 2 days ago, all in Enabled state with 90-day expiry. Old versions Disabled per rotation SOP. Scanner should filter disabled versions — only active versions relevant for compliance.
remediation_impact: Re-rotating already-rotated secrets disrupts dependent services during the rollback validation window.

scenario: IAM role saas-github-deploy with ecr:*, ecs:*, s3:* trusted by GitHub Actions OIDC. Scanner flags HIGH for deployment role with broad permissions assumable by GitHub OIDC.
why_misclassified: EC-09 (GitHub Actions deployment automation): OIDC trust is scoped with condition: StringLike token.actions.githubusercontent.com:sub repo:saas-company/saas-platform:environment:production. Only the production environment in the specific repository can assume the role. No human or other workflow can assume it.
detection_signal: IAM role saas-github-deploy: ecr:*, ecs:* trusted by token.actions.githubusercontent.com (GitHub OIDC)
ground_truth: OIDC trust condition: repo:saas-company/saas-platform:environment:production. Only production environment in the specific repo can assume. GitHub Actions OIDC + scoped conditions = short-lived, repository-scoped credentials. No long-lived keys.
remediation_impact: Restricting deployment role breaks production deployment pipeline, halting all new feature releases.

scenario: GCP org policy compute.requireOsLogin is enforced at org level. CSPM: compliant. However, saas-dev-tools project has project-level override disabling OS Login for a legacy automation tool.
why_misclassified: EC-40 (project override not checked): OS Login provides centralized SSH access control via GCP IAM. The project override re-enables metadata-based SSH keys for saas-dev-tools VMs. CSPM evaluates org policy but not project overrides.
detection_signal: Org policy compute.requireOsLogin: enforced. CSPM: compliant.
ground_truth: Project saas-dev-tools has constraint override disabling OS Login. VMs in this project accept metadata SSH keys bypassing GCP IAM SSH access control. Keys could be injected by anyone with compute.instances.setMetadata permission.
remediation_impact: SSH access to dev-tools VMs bypasses OS Login, allowing unauthorized SSH if metadata injection is achieved. Dev-tools VMs have service account access to production artifact buckets.

scenario: CSPM flags NACL saas-app-nacl for allowing all traffic (ALLOW ALL rule) on the application subnet. HIGH finding for insufficient subnet-level access control.
why_misclassified: EC-17 (NACL permissive, SG defense layer): Defense-in-depth applied at security group layer. All instances in subnet have SGs allowing only required ports from specific source SGs. Open NACL is intentional — SG layer provides the granular control per AWS well-architected framework guidance.
detection_signal: NACL saas-app-nacl rule 100: ALLOW ALL from 0.0.0.0/0
ground_truth: SGs on all instances: ALB SG → port 8080, Bastion SG → port 22. No NACL needed when SG rules are this specific. AWS WAF + SG layer covers the threat model. Open NACL is standard pattern for SG-managed subnets.
remediation_impact: Adding NACL rules alongside SG rules creates duplicate management without security benefit — changes must be maintained in two places.

scenario: ECR image saas-platform:v12.3.1 CVE scan passes. Scanner correctly identifies webpack, eslint, and typescript as devDependencies and suppresses their CVEs. However, the production bundle accidentally includes webpack's runtime.
why_misclassified: EC-43 inverse (devDep actually bundled): Webpack config added --mode development accidentally in a build config PR. Development mode embeds webpack-dev-server runtime in the bundle. CVE-2024-45590 (webpack-dev-server middleware prototype pollution) is present in production.
detection_signal: Scanner: webpack in devDependencies — CVE-2024-45590 suppressed. Production bundle not inspected.
ground_truth: Production Docker image contains webpack-dev-server runtime due to --mode development build flag. CVE-2024-45590 (prototype pollution) exploitable via crafted HMR requests. Scanner correctly suppressed the devDep CVE but did not inspect actual bundle.
remediation_impact: Prototype pollution in production API server allows request manipulation for affected tenants.

scenario: ECR image scan flags CVE-2024-3094 (XZ Utils backdoor, CVSS 10.0) in saas-pipeline:v4.1.0. Scanner requiring immediate remediation.
why_misclassified: EC-46 (CVE applicability condition not met): CVE-2024-3094 requires xz-utils 5.6.0-5.6.1 AND sshd linked to systemd's liblzma. SaaS pipeline container runs Alpine Linux with OpenRC init (not systemd). XZ backdoor condition not met on Alpine.
detection_signal: ECR scan: xz-utils 5.6.0 detected in saas-pipeline:v4.1.0 Alpine image. CVE-2024-3094 CVSS 10.0.
ground_truth: Alpine Linux uses musl libc and OpenRC, not systemd. CVE-2024-3094 exploit requires systemd-linked sshd (glibc-based). Alpine's sshd not linked against liblzma from xz-utils. NVD CPE analysis confirms Alpine not in affected configurations.
remediation_impact: Emergency rebuild of pipeline container for a conditionally inapplicable CVE creates unnecessary build churn.

scenario: GKE vulnerability scanner flags init container in saas-db-migration-pod for CVE-2024-21345 (CRITICAL) in the migration binary. Security team escalates for emergency patching.
why_misclassified: EC-30 (init container lifecycle): Migration init container runs only during pod startup (60 seconds) to apply DB schema changes. Terminates before main application container starts. Receives no network traffic. Exploit requires persistent access during the 60-second window.
detection_signal: CVE-2024-21345 CRITICAL in saas-db-migrate:v8 init container of saas-db-migration-pod
ground_truth: Init container: 60-second execution at pod cold start only. No network access (hostNetwork: false, no service endpoints during init phase). CVE exploitation would require pre-positioning in the init container execution context.
remediation_impact: Patching warranted but CRITICAL escalation overstates exploitation difficulty for a 60-second init-only window with no network exposure.

scenario: GCP Artifact Registry scan: CVE-2024-6387 marked as MODIFIED (OpenSSH) — scanner marks as addressed and clears the finding. A related unfixed variant CVE-2024-6409 (same component, different race condition) was published 5 days after the last scan.
why_misclassified: EC-46 (related CVE outside scan window): Scanner cleared CVE-2024-6387 finding and did not re-check the component for new CVEs within the 7-day scan window. CVE-2024-6409 missed due to feed staleness.
detection_signal: CVE-2024-6387: MODIFIED — no longer critical, cleared. No finding for CVE-2024-6409.
ground_truth: CVE-2024-6409 published after last scan — same OpenSSH signal handling race condition, CVSS 7.0 HIGH. Scanner clearing CVE-6387 did not trigger re-scan of the affected component for new CVEs.
remediation_impact: HIGH OpenSSH vulnerability in internet-facing SaaS infrastructure goes undetected due to related-CVE scan gap.

scenario: Azure API Management saas-apim-prod has no IP restriction policy on the gateway. Scanner flags HIGH for open API gateway that could be accessed by any IP.
why_misclassified: EC-05 (WAF-shielded): API Management is behind Azure Front Door with WAF policy saas-afd-waf. Front Door enforces DDoS protection, OWASP rules, and rate limiting. API Management is not directly accessible without passing through AFD+WAF.
detection_signal: Azure APIM saas-apim-prod: no IP filter policy configured at gateway level
ground_truth: Azure Front Door with WAF sits in front of APIM. Direct APIM access blocked by Azure Front Door's custom domain routing. AFD enforces authentication and WAF rules before requests reach APIM.
remediation_impact: Adding IP restriction at APIM level is redundant with Front Door+WAF enforcement and creates additional management overhead.

scenario: GCP SCC reports LOW for 'Service account has owner role' on SA saas-data-migration@saas-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com. Analyst ignores as LOW.
why_misclassified: EC-47 (CSP severity non-equivalence): GCP SCC rates Owner role on SA as LOW because it assumes the SA is intentionally privileged (common in migration contexts). AWS Security Hub and Azure Security Center would rate Owner/AdministratorAccess on a service account as CRITICAL. The SA is actively used in production pipelines.
detection_signal: GCP SCC: SA has Owner role — LOW severity (migration SA context assumed)
ground_truth: SA with Owner role actively used by data migration pipelines processing customer data. Owner role grants full project control. GCP LOW rating inappropriate for production SA with Owner. Actual risk is CRITICAL — Owner SA compromise = full tenant data access.
remediation_impact: LOW SLA (90+ days) for an active Owner-role SA. Real risk is immediate — SA should be downscoped to minimum required permissions.

scenario: Lambda function saas-legacy-export has CVE-2022-0536 (follow-redirects, HIGH) in package.json. Finding requests immediate patching. Function has 0 invocations in 200 days.
why_misclassified: EC-04 (dead code path): Lambda function had its trigger (S3 event) removed 200 days ago when feature was sunset. Reserved concurrency set to 0. Function is effectively dead — the vulnerability can never be triggered.
detection_signal: Lambda saas-legacy-export: follow-redirects 1.14.8 with CVE-2022-0536. 0 invocations in 200 days.
ground_truth: Reserved concurrency=0. No event source mapping. S3 trigger removed 2025-07-14. Function cannot execute. Decommission ticket pending legal hold review (export data audit trail).
remediation_impact: Patching a dead function consumes engineer time better spent on active vulnerabilities.

scenario: GCP IAM binding: external SA datadog-agent@datadog-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com has roles/monitoring.viewer on saas-prod project. Scanner flags HIGH for external service account access.
why_misclassified: EC-27 (trusted vendor integration): Datadog monitoring integration requires roles/monitoring.viewer for GCP infrastructure metrics collection. This is the documented Datadog GCP integration setup. Viewer role allows read-only metrics access — no data or configuration write access.
detection_signal: GCP IAM: external SA datadog-agent@datadog-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com has roles/monitoring.viewer
ground_truth: Datadog GCP integration requires this exact binding per Datadog documentation. Viewer role: read metrics/logs only. No access to customer data or GCP resource configuration. Vendor security review completed.
remediation_impact: Removing Datadog SA access breaks production monitoring for 380 microservices, eliminating alerting for latency and error rate regressions.

scenario: GCS bucket saas-customer-backups tagged security-reviewed=2025-01 suppresses CSPM findings per quarterly review policy. A new allUsers IAM binding was added by an automated migration script 3 weeks ago.
why_misclassified: EC-49 (suppression tag masking real issue): Quarterly review tag suppresses all findings for 90 days post-review. The allUsers binding occurred 3 weeks after the review — real exposure hidden behind review suppression.
detection_signal: Bucket saas-customer-backups: security-reviewed=2025-01 tag. CSPM suppression active.
ground_truth: allUsers storage.objects.viewer binding added 2026-01-05 by auto-migration-sa. Bucket contains customer data exports. 90-day suppression period masks the new exposure for 2 more months.
remediation_impact: Customer backup data publicly accessible for an extended period, violating GDPR data minimization and SOC 2 CC6.1.

scenario: CodeBuild project saas-security-scan has CVE-2024-28849 (follow-redirects, HIGH) in the node_modules used by the security scanning toolchain. Finding treats this as a production vulnerability.
why_misclassified: EC-02 (build layer only): CodeBuild project is the security scanning pipeline, not a production service. Node modules are used only during build-time scanning. CodeBuild environments are ephemeral and isolated. Vulnerability in build tool does not affect runtime application.
detection_signal: CodeBuild project saas-security-scan: follow-redirects 1.15.1 with CVE-2024-28849 in build environment
ground_truth: follow-redirects used by npm audit tool in the build pipeline. Build environment destroyed after each scan. No production artifact includes this library. Vulnerability is in the scanning tool, not in the application being scanned.
remediation_impact: Patching build tool is good practice but treating as production vulnerability creates false priority.

scenario: New AWS account saas-tenant-enterprise-12345 created 3 hours ago via Control Tower. CSPM shows no findings — SecurityHub findings still generating (warm-up window).
why_misclassified: EC-23 (warm-up window): Account provisioned without root MFA and default VPC present. Security Hub enrolled but has not yet run CIS benchmark. Warm-up gap means real baseline misconfigurations are invisible for up to 24 hours.
detection_signal: Account saas-tenant-enterprise-12345: SecurityHub enrolled 3h ago. No findings yet. CSPM: compliant.
ground_truth: Root account has no MFA (Control Tower account vending does not enforce root MFA by default). Default VPC present with open security groups. 3-hour window of unmonitored tenant account with root access.
remediation_impact: Enterprise customer tenant account with root-level access and open network during onboarding period. Real security baseline gap.

scenario: Macie scans RDS saas-internal-test-db and finds 2.1M records with email, name, and company matching PII patterns in the qa_test_data schema. GDPR finding generated.
why_misclassified: EC-20 (empty vault): Database is the internal QA automation test tenant, seeded with Faker-generated data. All emails use @qa.saas-internal.test domain (internal non-routable). Company names are fantasy companies from Faker.
detection_signal: Macie: email, name, company_name PII in saas-internal-test-db.qa_test_data (2.1M rows)
ground_truth: QA seed data uses Faker library. Domain @qa.saas-internal.test is company-internal and non-deliverable. No real customer data. All test accounts created and deleted by automation harness.
remediation_impact: Restricting QA test database access would block automated integration test suite, preventing deployment validation.

scenario: CSPM flags IAM access key AKIASAAS9876543210 as 105 days old without rotation, exceeding 90-day policy for saas-monitoring-svc user.
why_misclassified: EC-24 (stale scan cache): Key was rotated 11 days ago. New key AKIASAAS0123456789 active and used daily. Old key disabled. CSPM running on 14-day cache cycle shows the old key still as active.
detection_signal: IAM key AKIASAAS9876543210: created 105 days ago, last_used 11 days ago. CSPM: non-compliant.
ground_truth: AKIASAAS9876543210 disabled 11 days ago. AKIASAAS0123456789 created 11 days ago, used daily. Rotation completed within policy. Scanner cache delay misrepresents current state.
remediation_impact: Emergency re-rotation of already-rotated key causes service disruption for monitoring infrastructure.

scenario: CloudTrail log retention policy shows 365 days. CSPM marks compliant. However, the retention policy was changed from 365 to 30 days in a Terraform apply 89 days ago — the Terraform state file uses PST timestamps while the CSPM policy check uses UTC.
why_misclassified: EC-48 (timezone mismatch on policy evaluation): The 90-day lookback window for policy change detection uses PST timezone. The Terraform apply occurred at 2025-10-28T01:30:00-07:00 (PST) = 2025-10-28T08:30:00Z (UTC). UTC calculation shows 93 days since change, PST shows 92 days — both indicate recent change but CSPM only flags changes within 90 days.
detection_signal: CloudTrail retention: current_value=30 days. Change timestamp evaluated as 92 days ago (PST). Policy: flag changes within 90 days. Result: no flag.
ground_truth: UTC evaluation: 93 days since retention reduction. SOC 2 requires 1-year audit trail retention. Retention currently at 30 days — compliance gap. DST evaluation keeps it 2 days outside the detection window.
remediation_impact: 30-day log retention violates SOC 2 CC7.2 audit trail requirements. Real compliance gap active for 93 days without detection.

scenario: Vulnerability scanner finds CVE-2024-45338 HIGH in saas-api:v5.1.0 AND saas-api-shadow:v5.1.0 (shadow deployment for traffic mirroring). Security team opens 2 priority-1 tickets.
why_misclassified: EC-12 (shadow deployment duplicate): Shadow deployment mirrors production traffic for testing purposes but uses the identical container image. Single image, dual finding. Patching the image resolves both deployments. Two tickets for one remediation.
detection_signal: CVE HIGH in saas-api:v5.1.0 (100% traffic) AND saas-api-shadow:v5.1.0 (0% — mirror only). Same image tag.
ground_truth: saas-api-shadow uses identical image saas-api:v5.1.0 as the production deployment. Shadow receives mirrored traffic, returns no responses. Same image = single patching action. Finding deduplication by image digest warranted.
remediation_impact: 2 P1 tickets assigned when 1 is sufficient. Engineer capacity wasted on duplicate tracking.

scenario: GCP Artifact Registry SBOM for saas-tenant-api:v7.2.0 shows no CVEs. SBOM was generated from requirements.txt (Python). Actual installed packages differ due to pip's dependency resolver finding compatible sub-versions.
why_misclassified: EC-44 (SBOM from manifest vs installed env): requirements.txt specifies Pillow>=9.0.0. pip resolves to Pillow 9.0.0 (not the latest 10.x). CVE-2023-44271 (uncontrolled resource consumption in Pillow 9.0.x) present in resolved version but not detectable from requirements.txt manifest-based SBOM.
detection_signal: SBOM from requirements.txt: Pillow>=9.0.0 (no specific version). No CVE flagged.
ground_truth: pip install resolves Pillow==9.0.0 in production container. CVE-2023-44271 affects Pillow < 9.2.0. SBOM from requirements.txt cannot detect specific resolved version CVEs when version ranges specified.
remediation_impact: Image processing vulnerability in tenant API service allows resource exhaustion via crafted image uploads — potential DoS against multi-tenant platform.

scenario: CSPM flags shared-schema multi-tenant database saas-shared-rds as HIGH risk for tenant isolation failure — all tenants share the same RDS instance and database, with tenant_id as a discriminator column.
why_misclassified: EC-08 (VPC-bounded application isolation): Row-level security (RLS) enforced at the PostgreSQL layer using SET app.current_tenant_id. Every query runs with an active RLS policy that filters to the current tenant. No application query can access another tenant's rows.
detection_signal: RDS instance shared by all tenants in same database. No per-tenant schemas or databases detected.
ground_truth: PostgreSQL RLS policy tenant_isolation: USING (tenant_id = current_setting('app.current_tenant_id')). Policy applied to all tables containing tenant data. Application sets tenant context before any data access. Database architect review completed.
remediation_impact: Migrating to per-tenant databases would require architectural refactor affecting all 340 tenants — 12+ month project.

scenario: Azure API Management saas-apim allows HTTP traffic on gateway endpoint. Scanner flags MEDIUM for plaintext API access.
why_misclassified: EC-16 (edge-shielded redirect): APIM HTTP allowed for redirect purposes only. All HTTP requests to APIM are redirected to HTTPS via API policy with 301 response. Azure Front Door enforces HTTPS before reaching APIM. HTTP only used for the 301 redirect step.
detection_signal: Azure APIM: HTTP protocol enabled on gateway saas-apim-prod.azure-api.net
ground_truth: APIM inbound policy: if request.Url.Scheme == http then return-response with status 301 and Location: https://. All HTTPS enforced. AFD HTTPS-only enforced upstream.
remediation_impact: Disabling HTTP completely would break redirect for clients using HTTP URLs, degrading developer experience.

scenario: GCP DLP scan flags BigQuery analytics table saas-telemetry.session_events as containing user identifiers across 450M records. GDPR finding for large-scale PII processing.
why_misclassified: EC-22 (tokenization): session_id column contains BLAKE3 hashes of user UUID + session timestamp. user_id column stores SHA3-256 HMAC of the original user ID. No original identifiers stored. Processing is GDPR-compliant pseudonymization.
detection_signal: DLP scan: saas-telemetry.session_events — user_id (64-char hex) and session_id (64-char hex) match identifier patterns (450M rows)
ground_truth: All identifiers are cryptographic hashes with rotating HMAC keys (weekly rotation). Original user IDs not stored in telemetry dataset. GDPR Data Protection Officer confirmed pseudonymization standard met.
remediation_impact: Treating HMAC-hashed identifiers as PII would require GDPR consent for anonymized analytics, severely limiting platform improvement capabilities.

scenario: GCP SCC generates 3 separate HIGH findings for KMS key rotation not enabled — one for each region in a multi-region keyring (us-central1, europe-west1, asia-northeast1). 3 separate tickets created.
why_misclassified: EC-38 (cross-region duplicate): Single KMS keyring deployed to 3 regions for low-latency access. Enabling rotation on the primary key propagates to all regional replicas. 3 tickets for 1 remediation action.
detection_signal: KMS key rotation disabled: projects/saas-prod/locations/us-central1, europe-west1, asia-northeast1 (same key name)
ground_truth: Same KMS key deployed regionally for latency optimization. Single key rotation configuration fix propagates across all regions. Deduplication by key name across regions would collapse to 1 finding.
remediation_impact: 3x engineering effort for 1 KMS key rotation configuration change.

scenario: Lambda function saas-export-service has CVE-2024-45337 in a SFTP library. Feature flag 'sftp-export-enabled=true' shows 8% rollout. CSPM suppresses at below-10% threshold.
why_misclassified: EC-45 (enterprise tier partial rollout): 8% is the aggregate rollout — the flag is enabled for 100% of enterprise tier customers (which are 8% of total customer count). Enterprise customers have larger data volumes and the SFTP export processes the most sensitive data.
detection_signal: Feature flag sftp-export-enabled: 8% rollout. CSPM suppressed: below 10% threshold.
ground_truth: 100% of enterprise customers (8% of total = 27 enterprises) using SFTP export. These are the highest-value, most data-sensitive accounts. CVE-2024-45337 (SSH auth bypass) active for all enterprise SFTP exports.
remediation_impact: SSH auth bypass vulnerability active for all enterprise customers' SFTP exports — the most sensitive use case in the platform.

scenario: GCP Dataproc cluster saas-analytics-ephemeral-20260127 with 85 worker nodes created in 8 minutes. Anomaly detection flags potential account compromise via unauthorized compute provisioning.
why_misclassified: EC-10 (ephemeral analytics cluster): Dataproc cluster auto-created by Dataflow for large analytics job. Cluster tagged TTL=4h and linked to scheduled analytics job saas-quarterly-analytics. Pattern repeats quarterly.
detection_signal: 85 Dataproc worker nodes created in 8 minutes. GCP SCC: anomalous large-scale compute provisioning.
ground_truth: Quarterly analytics job saas-q4-customer-analysis requires 85 workers for 3-hour processing window. Cluster auto-deletes after completion. Scheduler job ID verifiable in Cloud Scheduler logs.
remediation_impact: Terminating quarterly analytics cluster would prevent Q4 2025 business intelligence reporting, delaying investor reports.

scenario: Amazon MQ broker saas-event-broker has a non-TLS AMQP listener on port 5672 within VPC. Scanner flags HIGH for unencrypted message transport.
why_misclassified: EC-13 (app-layer encryption): All messages are encrypted at the application layer before publishing. Message payloads are AES-256 encrypted with tenant-specific keys. Non-TLS AMQP transport within VPC carries only application-layer ciphertext.
detection_signal: Amazon MQ: AMQP port 5672 (non-TLS) accessible within VPC on saas-event-broker
ground_truth: Message payloads encrypted with AES-256 before publish. Even plaintext AMQP carries ciphertext. Port 5672 accessible only from app-tier SG within VPC. TLS listener on 5671 also available but app uses 5672 for lower latency within VPC.
remediation_impact: Forcing TLS on intra-VPC AMQP adds certificate management overhead for traffic that carries already-encrypted payloads.

scenario: Azure AD SP saas-legacy-partner-integration has last_sign_in=null (never signed in). CSPM classifies as inactive/headless, low risk. SP has Contributor role on 6 Azure subscriptions.
why_misclassified: EC-26 (never-used SP not inactive): SP created during partner onboarding 18 months ago. Integration never completed. SP has valid credentials (client secret expiry: 2027). Never-used does not mean safe — valid credential with Contributor access across 6 subscriptions exists.
detection_signal: SP saas-legacy-partner-integration: last_sign_in=null, created 18 months ago. CSPM: inactive, exempt.
ground_truth: Client secret valid until 2027. Contributor role on saas-prod, saas-staging, and 4 other subscriptions. Partner integration project was abandoned but SP was never decommissioned. Real lateral movement risk if credentials leaked.
remediation_impact: Valid Contributor-level SP credentials across 6 subscriptions with no monitoring. Compromise allows full infrastructure modification.

scenario: Azure Application Gateway saas-agw shows backend HTTP settings using port 80 for backend pool. Scanner flags HIGH for backend traffic traversing unencrypted HTTP to microservices.
why_misclassified: EC-41 (Azure managed TLS termination): Application Gateway terminates TLS at frontend and re-encrypts to backends using HTTPS. The HTTP backend setting in the console is a display artifact of the routing configuration label, not the actual transport protocol.
detection_signal: App Gateway saas-agw: BackendHttpSetting protocol=Http on backend pool saas-api-backends
ground_truth: Application Gateway configured with end-to-end SSL. Backend pool uses HTTPS with Azure-managed certificates. Protocol label in backend settings refers to the routing designation. Wireshark capture confirms TLS 1.3 on backend connections.
remediation_impact: Attempting to fix will break the App Gateway TLS re-encryption configuration.

scenario: Cloud Run service saas-api passes CVE checks. Jest is in devDependencies with CVE-2024-21538. Scanner suppresses jest CVE as devDependency. However, jest-worker is present in the production bundle.
why_misclassified: EC-43 inverse (devDep accidentally in production): Jest's jest-worker module was inadvertently included in webpack build due to a misconfigured external configuration. CVE-2024-21538 (ReDoS in jest-worker) present in production Cloud Run image despite being a devDependency in package.json.
detection_signal: jest in devDependencies — CVE-2024-21538 suppressed. Production image not analyzed for actual bundle contents.
ground_truth: webpack.config.js externals configuration accidentally removed jest-worker from externals list. jest-worker present in production bundle. SBOM from package.json misses the actual inclusion.
remediation_impact: ReDoS vulnerability in production service. Crafted request patterns could cause worker thread hang, impacting service availability.

scenario: CSPM reports HIGH for GCP project saas-tenant-acme missing audit log export. SOC 2 CC7.2 logging requirement appears unmet for the tenant project.
why_misclassified: EC-19 (org-level sink compensates): Organization-level log sink exports all _Required and _Default logs from all projects including saas-tenant-acme to centralized SIEM. CSPM checks project-level sinks only.
detection_signal: Project saas-tenant-acme: no project-level log export sink
ground_truth: Org-level log sink saas-org-audit exports all project audit logs to BigQuery and Cloud Storage. SOC 2 audit trail maintained centrally. ISO 27001 A.12.4.1 satisfied.
remediation_impact: Per-project sinks would duplicate logging costs across 340 tenant projects (~$28K/month additional).

scenario: RDS analytics replica saas-analytics-replica has publicly_accessible=true. Scanner flags CRITICAL for analytics database with potential PII accessible from internet.
why_misclassified: EC-37 (flag set for cross-VPC DNS, private subnet): Replica is in private subnet with only VPC peering routes. publicly_accessible=true set to enable DNS hostname resolution from analytics VPC peering partner. No route table path to internet.
detection_signal: RDS saas-analytics-replica: publicly_accessible=true
ground_truth: Private subnet, no IGW, no NAT gateway. VPC peering to analytics VPC requires DNS hostname resolution enabled. Route table confirms only RFC1918 routes. AWS Security Hub: No internet exposure path identified.
remediation_impact: Setting flag to false breaks analytics pipeline DNS resolution across VPC peering, disabling customer-facing analytics dashboards.

scenario: GCP SCC reports LOW for API server VM saas-api-prod-01 communicating with suspicious external IPs. Security Command Center Premium tier's threat intelligence integration applied LOW based on TI confidence score.
why_misclassified: EC-50 (enhanced controls severity inflation — inverse): SCC Premium TI integration applied LOW because the external IPs are in a 'gray' TI category (not definitively malicious). However, the communication pattern (30-second beacons to 3 IPs in 3 different countries) is anomalous for an API server that should only communicate with GCP services and customer IPs.
detection_signal: GCP SCC Premium: suspicious network activity to gray-zone TI IPs — LOW (TI confidence: 0.3)
ground_truth: API server communicating to IPs not in customer allowlist, GCP service ranges, or known CDN/DNS ranges. Beacon pattern: 30-second intervals. Production API server should have no outbound traffic to these IPs. Potential C2 despite non-definitive TI classification.
remediation_impact: Potential C2 beacon from production SaaS infrastructure goes uninvestigated due to low TI confidence score override.

scenario: API Gateway staging endpoint /debug/health-extended returns verbose system information including runtime, dependencies, and configuration. Scanner flags MEDIUM for information disclosure.
why_misclassified: EC-03 (intentionally enabled feature in staging): Debug endpoint is exclusively on the staging environment, accessible only from the internal engineering VPN IP range (172.16.0.0/12). The endpoint provides critical debugging context for the engineering team.
detection_signal: API Gateway /debug/health-extended: returns verbose response including Java version, Spring version, active profiles
ground_truth: Staging only. Access restricted to engineering VPN (172.16.0.0/12) via WAF IP restriction rule. No customer or external access. Intentional debugging feature for engineering team. No production equivalent exists.
remediation_impact: Removing staging debug endpoint would severely hamper engineers' ability to diagnose issues in the staging environment before production release.

scenario: EKS cluster audit logs show 28,000 Kubernetes API server authentication failures in 1 hour. GuardDuty Kubernetes threat detection flags as potential credential stuffing against EKS API.
why_misclassified: EC-06 (CIDR-gated known source): All authentication failures originate from the internal monitoring system (Prometheus/Kube-state-metrics) attempting to authenticate with an expired service account token after a token rotation. All requests from known internal CIDR 10.100.0.0/16.
detection_signal: EKS audit log: 28,000 auth failures, source IPs in 10.100.0.0/16, user-agent: kube-state-metrics
ground_truth: Service account token rotation occurred 2 hours ago. kube-state-metrics cached the old token and retried. All failures from known monitoring namespace SA. Pattern resolved after pod restart. No external IPs involved.
remediation_impact: Blocking monitoring SA access would eliminate platform observability for all customer-facing SLIs.

scenario: Azure VM saas-windows-report-server (Windows Server 2019) shows no CVE findings. Defender for Cloud applied the Linux patch assessment profile during a platform migration, skipping Windows-specific CVEs.
why_misclassified: EC-34 inverse (Windows CVEs missed on Windows VM): Azure Defender patch assessment profile migration accidentally assigned Linux profile to Windows VMs in the saas-reports resource group. CVE-2024-38063 and CVE-2024-43491 (both Windows-specific, CRITICAL) not evaluated.
detection_signal: Azure Defender: saas-windows-report-server — patch assessment profile: linux-cis. No Windows CVEs.
ground_truth: VM runs Windows Server 2019. CVE-2024-38063 (TCP/IP RCE, CVSS 9.8) and CVE-2024-43491 (Servicing Stack update, CVSS 9.8) applicable. Linux patch profile misassigned during Azure VM fleet migration.
remediation_impact: Two CRITICAL Windows CVEs on production reporting server go unpatched due to profile misassignment.

scenario: API Gateway stage saas-api-v1 has missing WAF, no authentication on legacy endpoints, and deprecated OAuth 2.0 flows. Scanner generates multiple HIGH findings requiring remediation.
why_misclassified: EC-11 (sunset service): API v1 stage has usage plan set to 0 requests/month. All customers migrated to v3. DNS CNAME no longer points to v1 stage. Stage maintained for 6-month documentation window only. Zero customer traffic in 210 days.
detection_signal: API Gateway saas-api-v1: no WAF, deprecated auth flows, usage plan=0 requests/month, 0 invocations in 210 days
ground_truth: Stage is a dead configuration artifact with 0 traffic. All customers on v3. v1 DNS removed. Pending deletion after 6-month SDK migration documentation period expires 2026-04-01.
remediation_impact: Emergency remediation of a zero-traffic sunset stage wastes engineering effort better applied to active infrastructure.

scenario: Lambda function saas-sso-handler uses vendored fork of passport.js authentication library. SBOM marks as vendor-managed, CVE analysis skipped. Fork is 16 months old.
why_misclassified: EC-42 (vendored fork not patched): CVE-2024-37897 (authentication bypass in passport.js session handling) disclosed 5 months ago. The internal fork predates this CVE. Vendor directory skipped in SBOM analysis.
detection_signal: vendor/passport/ in saas-sso-handler. SBOM: vendor-managed, skip.
ground_truth: vendor/passport/lib/session.js contains the vulnerable session handling code. CVE-2024-37897 allows authentication bypass via crafted session cookie. SSO handler is critical path for all 340 tenant logins.
remediation_impact: Authentication bypass in SSO handler — CRITICAL for all tenant logins. Attacker could bypass authentication for any tenant.

scenario: GCP SA saas-deploy@saas-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com has roles/iam.serviceAccountUser on all SAs in the project. Scanner flags HIGH for SA impersonation risk.
why_misclassified: EC-15 (IAM condition bound permission): The roles/iam.serviceAccountUser binding has condition: resource.name matches projects/saas-prod/serviceAccounts/saas-app-* limiting impersonation to app-specific SAs only. Not a blanket SA user grant.
detection_signal: GCP IAM: saas-deploy SA has roles/iam.serviceAccountUser on project level
ground_truth: IAM condition: resource.name.startsWith('projects/saas-prod/serviceAccounts/saas-app-') limits scope to application SAs. Platform and admin SAs (saas-platform-*, saas-admin-*) excluded by naming convention condition.
remediation_impact: Removing deployment SA user permission breaks Cloud Run deployment automation that requires SA attachment.

scenario: GCP org policy run.allowedIngress restricts Cloud Run to internal-only traffic at org level. CSPM: compliant. However, project saas-integrations has override enabling all traffic.
why_misclassified: EC-40 (project override not traversed): CSPM evaluates org policy at org level — compliant. Integration project override allows allUsers ingress for a Cloud Run service that handles customer webhook deliveries, but also inadvertently exposes an internal admin Cloud Run service.
detection_signal: Org policy run.allowedIngress=internal. CSPM: compliant.
