ground_truth: Project override: run.allowedIngress=all in saas-integrations. Two Cloud Run services exposed: saas-webhook-delivery (intentional) AND saas-admin-panel (inadvertent). Admin panel has no authentication — assumed internal-only via org policy.
remediation_impact: Internal admin panel for managing tenant configurations exposed to internet without authentication.

scenario: IAM role saas-db-migration-role has rds:* and iam:PassRole permissions. Scanner flags HIGH for database management role with IAM pass capabilities.
why_misclassified: EC-09 (automation role — scoped deployment): Role is assumed only by the database migration ECS task during deployment windows. iam:PassRole scoped to rds-monitoring-role ARN only (CloudWatch RDS monitoring). rds:* scoped to production cluster ARN. Role assumed 2-4x per deployment via CI/CD OIDC only.
detection_signal: IAM role saas-db-migration-role: rds:*, iam:PassRole on Resource:*
ground_truth: iam:PassRole restricted to specific monitoring role ARN via condition. rds:* restricted to specific RDS cluster ARN. Role trusts only the migration ECS task ARN via OIDC. Deployment automation role with appropriate scope.
remediation_impact: Restricting migration role would break database schema migration automation, requiring manual DBA intervention for every deployment.

scenario: CSPM flags GCP SA saas-analytics-reader as having a key 98 days old, exceeding 90-day rotation policy. Key belongs to analytics read-only service account.
why_misclassified: EC-25 (key in disabled rotation state): Key was rotated 7 days ago via automated rotation script. Old key is DISABLED (not deleted) per 14-day grace period policy. Scanner reports creation date of disabled key (98 days) rather than checking active key age (7 days).
detection_signal: SA saas-analytics-reader: key creation date = 98 days ago. Rotation policy: 90 days.
ground_truth: Old key (98 days, DISABLED since day 91). New key (7 days, ENABLED). Rotation completed 7 days ago. Scanner should filter disabled keys from rotation age calculation.
remediation_impact: Re-rotating already-rotated SA key causes analytics pipeline disruption during grace period.

scenario: Azure Security Center reports MEDIUM for 'AKS cluster has Kubernetes dashboard enabled' on saas-aks-prod. Same finding on GCP GKE would be HIGH, and on Amazon EKS would be HIGH.
why_misclassified: EC-47 (CSP severity non-equivalence): Azure rates Kubernetes dashboard exposure as MEDIUM because Azure Dashboard has RBAC in newer versions. However, the specific AKS version deployed (1.27) still uses the legacy dashboard without sufficient RBAC enforcement.
detection_signal: Azure Security Center: AKS saas-aks-prod — Kubernetes dashboard enabled — MEDIUM
ground_truth: AKS 1.27 Kubernetes dashboard uses legacy auth that can be bypassed. GCP and AWS rate similar findings HIGH. The dashboard exposes cluster admin UI on an internal port reachable from the cluster network. Multi-tenant risk.
remediation_impact: MEDIUM SLA (30 days) for a dashboard with legacy auth on a multi-tenant production cluster. Azure's lower baseline rating understates risk.

scenario: Macie analysis of Kinesis stream saas-usage-events flags PII — user identifier and feature usage data detected in the stream. 15M events/day flagged as GDPR-regulated personal data.
why_misclassified: EC-20 (anonymized data): user_id in usage events is a surrogate token (daily-rotating SHA-256 HMAC). No cross-day linkability. Feature usage data is aggregated at 5-minute granularity — individual user behavior unrecoverable. GDPR Article 11 anonymization standard met.
detection_signal: Kinesis stream saas-usage-events: user_id field (64-char hex), feature_name, timestamp (15M events/day)
ground_truth: user_id is daily-rotating HMAC — no cross-session linkability. 5-minute event aggregation. GDPR Data Protection Officer and external DPA consultant confirmed anonymization standard. No re-identification possible.
remediation_impact: Treating anonymized usage metrics as PII would require GDPR consent for all product analytics, eliminating the behavioral data needed for platform improvement.

scenario: GCP Pub/Sub topic saas-events allows allAuthenticatedUsers to publish. Scanner flags HIGH for broad publish access on production event stream.
why_misclassified: EC-18 (VPC Service Controls deny compensates): Pub/Sub IAM appears open but VPC Service Controls perimeter restricts allAuthenticatedUsers to only identities within the GCP organization. External Google accounts cannot publish despite the broad IAM binding.
detection_signal: Pub/Sub topic saas-events: allAuthenticatedUsers has roles/pubsub.publisher
ground_truth: VPC Service Controls perimeter saas-sc-perimeter includes Pub/Sub and applies iam.allowedPolicyMemberDomains constraint. Only @saas-company.com identities qualify as allAuthenticatedUsers within the perimeter.
remediation_impact: Restricting Pub/Sub IAM would require enumerating all internal service accounts and users that publish to the topic — management overhead for ephemeral workloads.

scenario: Azure AD application saas-enterprise-connector has compliance-reviewed=2025-Q3 tag. CSPM suppresses findings. A new Graph API permission (Sites.ReadWrite.All) was added 3 weeks ago.
why_misclassified: EC-49 (suppression tag masking real issue): Q3 2025 compliance review approved Sites.Read.All. New Sites.ReadWrite.All permission added via Azure Portal by a developer 3 weeks after the review. Suppression still active for full Q4 2025 review cycle.
detection_signal: App saas-enterprise-connector: tag compliance-reviewed=2025-Q3. CSPM suppression active.
ground_truth: Application now has Sites.ReadWrite.All (full SharePoint read/write for all site collections). Q3 review approved read-only Sites.Read.All. Write permission added post-review without additional review. Suppression hides the upgrade.
remediation_impact: SaaS connector with full SharePoint write access to enterprise customer tenants. Potential for unauthorized document modification across all enterprise customers.

scenario: AWS GuardDuty flags 200 EC2 instances launched simultaneously in the staging account as potential account compromise. Same instance type, same AMI, launched by the same IAM role.
why_misclassified: EC-10 (ephemeral CI testing fleet): Instances are CI/CD parallel test runners launched for the integration test suite. All tagged CIJob=true, TTL=90min. Auto-terminated when tests complete. Launched 3 times/week for regression testing.
detection_signal: 200 EC2 t3.medium instances launched simultaneously from IAM role saas-ci-runner-role in staging account
ground_truth: Integration test suite requires 200 parallel runners for 90-minute test window. Pattern repeats 3x/week (Mon/Wed/Fri). Instances auto-terminate. No data access beyond isolated test database. IDs in CI job manifest.
remediation_impact: Terminating CI test fleet would fail the regression test suite and block production deployments.

scenario: New ECS service saas-billing-v3 deployed 2 hours ago shows 0% patch compliance score. Security team escalates for immediate patching before service handles any billing traffic.
why_misclassified: EC-23 (warm-up window): Service deployed from golden AMI built 3 days ago with all patches current. Patch compliance scan runs every 24 hours. 0% reflects absence of initial scan, not actual missing patches. Service pre-approved via AMI compliance review.
detection_signal: ECS service saas-billing-v3: PatchComplianceScore=0 (not yet scanned)
ground_truth: AMI ami-0saas-billing-v3 built 3 days ago from patched base. AMI compliance scan passed (score: 97%). ECS task compliance assessment pending first scan cycle in 22 hours. 0 = not yet evaluated.
remediation_impact: Patching a freshly deployed service built from a compliant AMI is unnecessary and risks service stability during the billing migration period.

scenario: GCP firewall rules for saas-prod VPC appear compliant per CSPM (last scan 11 days ago). An engineer added a temporary debug rule 8 days ago opening port 8080 to 0.0.0.0/0 for troubleshooting.
why_misclassified: EC-24 (stale scan): Debug firewall rule added between 14-day scan cycles. Rule never removed after troubleshooting concluded. Admin API port 8080 exposed to internet for 8 days.
detection_signal: CSPM last scan: 11 days ago (clean). Firewall rule added 8 days ago: allow-debug-8080, allow-all, port 8080 — not in CSPM cache.
ground_truth: Firewall rule allow-debug-8080 added by engineer for debugging. Port 8080 is the microservice admin API with internal management endpoints. Exposed to internet for 8 days without detection.
remediation_impact: Admin API endpoints accessible from internet for 8+ days. Admin API includes tenant management operations.

scenario: API Gateway endpoint /health returns server information including version, dependencies, and uptime. Scanner flags MEDIUM for information disclosure that could aid attackers.
why_misclassified: EC-16 (edge-shielded + intentional): Health endpoint is intentionally public for load balancer health checks and status page integrations. Returns only non-sensitive operational status. AWS WAF rate-limits the endpoint to prevent reconnaissance scraping.
detection_signal: GET /health returns: {version: '4.1.2', runtime: 'node20', uptime: 1234567, status: 'healthy'}
ground_truth: Version information is public in release notes and npm registry. Runtime info not exploitable without additional vulns. WAF rate-limits to 60 req/min. Standard SaaS health endpoint pattern required by AWS ALB health checks and 3rd party status monitors.
remediation_impact: Removing version from health endpoint breaks 14 status monitoring integrations and ALB health check expectations.

scenario: DLP scan flags staging BigQuery table saas-staging-analytics.test_events as containing PII — user emails, IP addresses, and session data in 8M records.
why_misclassified: EC-21 (synthetic staging data): Staging analytics populated from Faker-generated synthetic events. Email domain @staging.saas-test.invalid. IP addresses are RFC5737 documentation ranges (192.0.2.0/24, 198.51.100.0/24). Session data has deterministic patterns.
detection_signal: DLP: saas-staging-analytics.test_events — email, IP address patterns detected (8M rows)
ground_truth: Staging data seeded by saas-staging-seeder using Faker and documentation IP ranges. No real user data. IP ranges 192.0.2.x and 198.51.100.x are TEST-NET ranges per RFC5737.
remediation_impact: Restricting staging analytics access blocks the QA team from validating analytics features.

scenario: DLP scan flags DynamoDB table saas-audit-trail for containing unique identifiers linked to users — specifically account_id and event_correlation_id fields across 850M records.
why_misclassified: EC-22 (tokenization): account_id is a UUIDv4 surrogate with no cross-reference table. event_correlation_id is a BLAKE2b hash of the event content. Neither field can be linked to a natural person without the mapping table stored in a separate, more restricted service.
detection_signal: DLP: UUIDv4 patterns in DynamoDB saas-audit-trail (850M items). Possible unique identifiers.
ground_truth: account_id UUIDs have no mapping table in the audit trail database or its data model. event_correlation_id is a content hash. GDPR anonymization confirmed by external DPA consultant — no re-identification path from audit trail alone.
remediation_impact: Treating UUID surrogate keys as PII would require rearchitecting the audit trail, destroying its forensic utility.

scenario: ECR image scan: CVE-2024-23827 marked as DISPUTED/WITHDRAWN — scanner clears the finding and removes the component from watch list. Three days later CVE-2024-28849 for the same follow-redirects version is published.
why_misclassified: EC-46 (related CVE outside watch window): When CVE withdrawn, scanner removes follow-redirects 1.15.4 from active watch. New CVE-2024-28849 (HIGH, SSRF in follow-redirects 1.x) published after the scan — caught in the 3-day gap between CVE publication and next scan cycle.
detection_signal: CVE-2024-23827: WITHDRAWN — cleared. follow-redirects 1.15.4 removed from watchlist. CVE-2024-28849: not yet in scanner feed.
ground_truth: follow-redirects 1.15.4 has CVE-2024-28849 (SSRF, HIGH, published 3 days after scan). Component cleared from watchlist due to prior CVE withdrawal. 3-day feed lag means new CVE missed.
remediation_impact: SSRF in HTTP redirect library used by Lambda integration functions. New vulnerability missed due to CVE withdrawal clearing component from active monitoring.

scenario: Azure Security Center flags external SP new-relic-monitoring@newrelic-azure-prod.onmicrosoft.com has Monitoring Reader on saas-prod subscription. Scanner flags HIGH for external tenant SP access.
why_misclassified: EC-27 (trusted vendor integration): New Relic Azure monitoring integration requires Monitoring Reader for infrastructure metrics. External tenant SP is New Relic's documented integration SA. Monitoring Reader is read-only metrics access — no data or config write capability.
detection_signal: External SP new-relic-monitoring: Monitoring Reader on saas-prod subscription (external tenant)
ground_truth: New Relic Azure monitoring integration per New Relic docs. Monitoring Reader: read-only metrics/logs. No customer data access. Vendor security review completed. SOC 2 compliance verified for New Relic.
remediation_impact: Removing New Relic SP access disables production infrastructure monitoring, eliminating alerts for latency regressions and error spikes.

scenario: Azure Defender for Storage flags staging storage account saas-staging-uploads as HIGH for 'Malware detected in uploaded blob'. Same finding would be MEDIUM on AWS S3 with Macie.
why_misclassified: EC-47 (CSP severity non-equivalence): Azure Defender applies HIGH for any malware detection regardless of environment context. Staging account, no production traffic, synthetic test data. AWS would apply environment context multiplier. Azure does not.
detection_signal: Azure Defender: malware detected in saas-staging-uploads container 'test-uploads'. Severity: HIGH.
ground_truth: Staging account used to test malware scanning pipeline itself — test team uploads EICAR test file to verify scanner works. EICAR is a harmless test file, not actual malware. Azure Defender HIGH is appropriate for production but not for intentional test-file uploads in staging.
remediation_impact: HIGH SLA (7-day) for an intentional EICAR test file in a staging environment wastes security team capacity.

scenario: GCP CSPM flags 4 reserved external IP addresses as unattached, recommending deletion to reduce attack surface.
why_misclassified: EC-07 (intentionally reserved DR IPs): External IPs are reserved for disaster recovery scenarios and pre-registered in enterprise customer firewall allowlists. Releasing would require customer notification and allowlist updates during an emergency.
detection_signal: GCP Compute: 4 reserved external IPs with status=RESERVED (not attached) for 90-180 days
ground_truth: IPs registered in DR runbook. Enterprise customers (340) have these IPs in their corporate firewall allowlists for SaaS API access during DR failover. Releasing requires updating all customer firewall policies.
remediation_impact: Releasing DR IPs destroys failover capability and requires updating 340 enterprise customer firewall configurations.

scenario: EKS pod saas-parser-svc uses distroless/python3.11. Scanner detects CVE-2023-44271 in Pillow (AV:N, uncontrolled resource consumption) and applies EC-29 distroless downgrade pattern, reducing to LOW.
why_misclassified: EC-29 (distroless pattern over-applied): CVE-2023-44271 is AV:N with no shell requirement — it's a resource exhaustion attack via crafted PNG uploads to the web API. Distroless provides no protection for application-layer CVEs that execute through the application code path.
detection_signal: Pillow CVE-2023-44271 downgraded LOW — distroless image detected. AV:N exploitability assumed reduced.
ground_truth: saas-parser-svc accepts image uploads from customers. CVE-2023-44271 exploitable by uploading a crafted PNG that causes Pillow to consume excessive memory. No shell needed. Application-layer vulnerability unaffected by distroless.
remediation_impact: DoS vulnerability in customer-facing image parsing service. Crafted PNG upload can cause OOM, crashing the parser pod and impacting all tenants sharing the node.

scenario: S3 bucket saas-docs-public allows public read. Scanner flags MEDIUM for public S3 bucket in production AWS account.
why_misclassified: EC-05 (intentionally public + edge-shielded): Bucket hosts public API documentation, SDK download packages, and release notes. Intentionally public for developer customers to access docs without authentication. CloudFront OAC controls access. No sensitive content.
detection_signal: S3 bucket saas-docs-public: BlockPublicAcls=false, public read on /docs/* prefix
ground_truth: Bucket contains only public-facing developer documentation (OpenAPI specs, SDK zips, changelog). Content reviewed for sensitivity before publication. No customer data, no configuration, no secrets. Public access by design.
remediation_impact: Making documentation private would break developer onboarding workflow and SDK download automation for 8,200 developers.

scenario: Azure PIM eligible role 'Owner on saas-prod' activated 31 times in 45 days. CSPM does not flag because PIM eligible roles are in the approved break-glass list. Historical rate: 2 activations per quarter.
why_misclassified: EC-28 (break-glass frequency anomaly): Break-glass exemption correctly applies to PIM eligible roles. However, 31 activations in 45 days (vs. 2/quarter baseline) is 31x above normal. No anomaly detection on exempted PIM activation frequency.
detection_signal: PIM Owner activation: 31 times in 45 days. Role in break-glass exemption list — no finding.
ground_truth: Normal rate: ~8/year. Current: 31/45 days = 250/year equivalent. 28 of 31 activations by same AAD user correlating with large S3-equivalent Azure Blob operations during off-hours. Insider threat or compromised admin account pattern.
remediation_impact: Potential insider threat using break-glass elevation to exfiltrate customer data. PIM activation frequency anomaly detection required.

scenario: GCP Security Command Center flags 18 Cloud Run services for not using customer-managed encryption keys. Services are the core SaaS microservices processing customer requests.
why_misclassified: EC-39 (serverless encryption nuance): Cloud Run services are encrypted with Google-managed keys by default. Finding is CMK absence, not encryption absence. Google-managed AES-256 encryption satisfies SOC 2 CC6.1. CMK only required for services handling highly sensitive data requiring customer-controlled key revocation.
detection_signal: 18 Cloud Run services: customerManagedEncryptionKey=null
ground_truth: All Cloud Run services use Google-managed AES-256 encryption. SOC 2 encryption at rest: satisfied. CMK required only for saas-pii-processor and saas-backup services (already have CMK). 18 flagged services handle API logic without persistent sensitive data.
remediation_impact: Adding CMK to 18 services adds $9K/month Cloud KMS costs and key rotation complexity.

scenario: ECS service saas-auth-blue (inactive deployment slot) has 8 HIGH CVEs in nodejs18 base. Scanner requests emergency patching. Service is part of a blue-green deployment pattern.
why_misclassified: EC-12 (inactive blue-green slot): ALB routes 100% traffic to saas-auth-green (nodejs20, fully patched). Blue slot has desired_count=1 (warm standby) but receives 0% ALB traffic. Will be replaced at next deployment.
detection_signal: ECS service saas-auth-blue: nodejs18 base image with 8 HIGH CVEs. Desired count: 1.
ground_truth: saas-auth-blue is inactive (0% ALB weight). Warm standby kept for 15-minute rollback capability. Image will be replaced at next deployment cycle (2 days). Patching inactive slot provides minimal value given imminent replacement.
remediation_impact: Patching inactive standby that will be replaced in 2 days consumes engineer capacity with minimal security benefit.

scenario: GKE cluster saas-prod has Binary Authorization enabled (CSPM compliant). However, the policy evaluationMode was switched to DRYRUN_AUDIT_LOG_ONLY during an upgrade 2 weeks ago.
why_misclassified: EC-35 (admission enforcement gap): CSPM checks binaryAuthorization.enabled=true but not the evaluationMode. Dry-run mode logs violations without blocking. Three unsigned SaaS microservice images deployed in the past week.
detection_signal: GKE: binaryAuthorization.enabled=true. CSPM: compliant. evaluationMode not inspected.
ground_truth: evaluationMode=DRYRUN_AUDIT_LOG_ONLY. Policy violations logged in Cloud Audit Logs but deployments not blocked. 3 unsigned images deployed without policy enforcement.
remediation_impact: Supply chain integrity enforcement disabled. Unsigned images in production with no blocking enforcement.

scenario: Azure App Service saas-legacy-importer has CVE-2024-38094 (SharePoint RCE) in Microsoft.SharePoint.Client.dll. Security team escalates for emergency patching.
why_misclassified: EC-04 (dead code): SharePoint client library included from 8 months ago during a migration attempt. Migration switched to Microsoft Graph API. SharePoint client library methods are never called. Feature flag SharepointClientEnabled=false prevents code path execution.
detection_signal: Azure App Service: Microsoft.SharePoint.Client.dll with CVE-2024-38094 in dependency scan
ground_truth: SharePoint client code surrounded by if(config.SharepointClientEnabled) check, which is always false. Library loaded by .NET DLL loader but SharePoint methods never invoked. Dead code confirmed by code coverage analysis (0% for SharePoint namespace).
remediation_impact: Removing dead library is good housekeeping but HIGH emergency urgency overstated for unreachable code.

scenario: AWS Security Hub reports MEDIUM for 'RDS instance uses default parameter group' on saas-customer-db. Same finding on Azure would be HIGH, on GCP would be HIGH.
why_misclassified: EC-47 (CSP severity non-equivalence): Security Hub rates default parameter group as MEDIUM, assuming it's a best-practice gap. For a multi-tenant SaaS production database, default PostgreSQL parameter group means query logging, slow query logging, and connection logging are all disabled — a real SOC 2 audit logging gap.
detection_signal: Security Hub: RDS saas-customer-db uses default parameter group — MEDIUM
ground_truth: Default parameter group disables log_statement, log_min_duration_statement, and log_connections. Without these, SQL injection attempts and unauthorized data access queries go unlogged. SOC 2 CC7.2 audit logging not satisfied. Real HIGH for multi-tenant production DB.
remediation_impact: MEDIUM SLA (30 days) for an active audit logging gap on a multi-tenant production database. Unauthorized queries could go undetected for 30 days.

scenario: GuardDuty flags 45,000 Unauthorized API calls in 1 hour against the SaaS platform API. Pattern analyzed as potential DDoS or brute force attack.
why_misclassified: EC-06 (CIDR-gated expected pattern): All 45K failures originate from known load balancer health check IPs making calls with expired JWT tokens. JWT tokens expire after 1 hour. Health check interval: 5 seconds × 15 LB nodes × 60 min × 10 endpoints = 54,000 calls/hour. Matches expected rate.
detection_signal: GuardDuty: 45,000 HTTP 401 Unauthorized on saas-api-prod in 1 hour
ground_truth: ALB health checks use cached JWT from initial token exchange. Health check frequency × endpoints × nodes = expected failure count. Source IPs: ALB health check range (10.0.0.0/8). Resolved by updating health check to use a dedicated health token.
remediation_impact: Investigation cost for expected ALB health check behavior. Root cause: health check misconfiguration, not an attack.

scenario: GCP Cloud Function saas-webhook-dispatcher flagged for CVE-2024-24783 in the Go TLS runtime layer. Finding requests migration to newer Go runtime.
why_misclassified: EC-36 (managed runtime shared responsibility): Cloud Function Go runtime is managed by Google. GCP patches managed runtime layers transparently. Customer code runs in an isolated function environment above the managed runtime. Customer cannot and should not patch GCP-managed runtime components.
detection_signal: Cloud Function saas-webhook-dispatcher: runtime go119 — CVE-2024-24783 in Go TLS standard library
ground_truth: Go 1.19 managed runtime patched by GCP. CVE in managed runtime layer is GCP responsibility. Customer code uses only standard HTTP client — not the specific TLS code path vulnerable to CVE-2024-24783 (certificate chain validation).
remediation_impact: Customer cannot patch GCP managed runtime. Migrating to go121 is a good practice update but CRITICAL urgency is misplaced.
